d: Guidelines for implementing preset systems that comply with Roblox Community Standards and Terms of Use.
h:
Preset systems let users safely send predefined text to each other to coordinate gameplay. They can be implemented in a variety of ways, such as wheels that let users select and send presets publicly to one another in-game.

These systems must not be used to enable unrestricted, real-time, two-way communication between players of different ages or to bypass platform safety systems. They are meant to:

  • Support quick in-game coordination
  • Reduce friction in common gameplay moments
  • Preserve Roblox's existing safety and age-based communication protections

Roblox's built-in Quick Words system is a preset system that already complies with these guidelines. Use it to add custom Quick Words without building your own preset system.

Guidelines

If you want to implement this type of system, you must adhere to these guidelines, which are meant to help you comply with our Community Standards and Terms of Use.

Safety first

Preset systems must reinforce existing Roblox safety features – not work around them. If the preset system enables dynamic conversation, then it undermines platform safety and doesn't comply with our policies.

Ask yourself: Does this feature break, bypass, or circumvent any existing Roblox safety features by enabling free-form, two-way, directed, and dynamic conversation? If it does, the system must respect the requirements that users be age checked (through Facial Age Estimation or ID-verification) and of a similar age to chat.

If the system you want to implement is purely to help players communicate in-game actions, confirmations, or basic reactions, you can use a preset system that lets users send presets to each other regardless of age or age check status.

Intent, not conversation

Preset systems are for expressing immediate gameplay intent, not dialog. Each preset must stand alone and be complete without requiring a response unrelated to gameplay. General back and forth calls-to-action and replies such as "Help" followed by an "OK" are acceptable.

Presets must:

  • Be relevant to the current game mode or scenario
  • Avoid open-ended or socially exploratory language
  • Ideally expire quickly or lose relevance outside the moment

Presets must not:

  • Include slang that could carry hidden or evolving meanings
  • Reference to real-world contact, identity, or relationships
  • Involve emotional manipulation, social pressure, or content that would violate Roblox's Community Standards

Examples

  • ✅ "Need help"
  • ✅ "Defending this area"
  • ✅ "Ready"
  • ❌ "Why didn't you help me?"
  • ❌ "Do you like me?"

Limited, finite Scope

Preset systems must not gain meaning when combined, repeated, or sequenced. They should be tied to the current game context and lose relevance outside the moment. If players can use the wheel to "say anything, just slower," the design is not permitted.

Examples

  • ✅ "Pass the ball"
  • ✅ "Reloading"
  • ✅ "Enemy nearby"
  • ❌ "Where are you from?"
  • ❌ "What are your socials?"

Enforcement and review

All content and related features may be reviewed by Roblox to ensure compliance with our guidelines and to protect users on the platform. This may include:

  • Reviewing preset system content during game review
  • Requiring changes or removal if a system enables circumvention or otherwise violates Roblox's Community Standards
  • Disabling preset system features that undermine platform safety goals
  • Taking additional enforcement actions taken on your game, account, or group

Creators are responsible for ensuring that all content and future updates continue to comply with these guidelines.

Requirements

All preset systems and their features must adhere to the following requirements:

  • All UI of presets must be properly labeled as system preset when displaying within chat
  • All preset systems should be visually distinct from Roblox's native freeform chat
  • Presets should not incorporate any end marks or terminal punctuation, such as exclamation marks, question marks, or periods, to prevent them from being confused with general chat messages
  • All presets must go through TextService:FilterStringAsync()
  • Add a rate-limit (10 seconds per send)
  • Limit the number of presets displayed to 12 or less for your Universe

What is allowed

Preset systems may include:

  • Tactical gameplay commands (e.g., "Attack", "Defend", "Hold Position")
  • Cooperative commands (e.g., "Follow me", "Ready", "Wait")
  • Sports/FPS-style callouts (e.g., "Reloading", "Cover me", "Nice shot")
  • Neutral encouragement or game statements (e.g., "Well played", "Thanks")

These should always be finite, curated, and creator-controlled.

What is not allowed

Preset systems may not be used to:

  • Simulate free-form chat or conversation
  • Compliment or flatter others with statements that don't relate to gameplay
  • Enable back-and-forth dialogue across age groups
  • Encode custom messages
  • Circumvent chat, DM, or voice restrictions
  • Replace or mirror unrestricted social features
  • Questions or social questions

Examples of disallowed patterns:

  • Alphabet wheels or number-based encoding
  • Question/answer structures ("Why?", "Because")
  • "Hi!" "Hello!" "How are you?" "What's up?"

kid.simple: A preset system lets players send ready-made messages, like "Need help" or "Reloading", often by picking from a wheel. Because anyone can use them, even players who cannot free-chat, Roblox has strict rules: presets must be about gameplay, not conversation. This page explains what phrases are allowed, what is banned, and the technical requirements like filtering and rate limits. If you want this feature, Roblox's built-in Quick Words already follows all the rules.
kid.analogy: It is like hand signals in a sports team: "pass", "cover me", "ready". They help the team play, but you could never use them to have a real conversation about your weekend.
keyPoints: Presets are for quick gameplay coordination, not for chatting. They must not let players of different ages have free, two-way conversations or get around safety systems.
Each preset must stand alone, fit the current game moment, and avoid open-ended or social language. Simple call and reply like "Help" then "OK" is fine.
Good examples: "Need help", "Defending this area", "Ready", "Pass the ball", "Reloading", "Enemy nearby".
Bad examples: "Why didn't you help me?", "Do you like me?", "Where are you from?", "What are your socials?", greetings like "Hi!" and "How are you?".
No alphabet wheels, number codes, or combos that let players spell out any message.

Requirements: label presets as system preset in chat, make them look different from normal chat, use no end punctuation (no ! ? or .), filter them with `TextService:FilterStringAsync()`, rate-limit to one send per 10 seconds, and show 12 presets or fewer.
Roblox may review your preset system and require changes, disable it, or take action on your game, account, or group if it breaks the rules.
Roblox's built-in Quick Words already follows these guidelines, so you can use it instead of building your own.

terms.preset: A message written ahead of time by the game creator that players can pick and send, like "Ready".
terms.preset system: The feature, like a wheel or menu, that lets players send presets.
terms.two-way communication: A real back-and-forth conversation between players.
terms.circumvent: To get around a rule or safety system on purpose.
terms.age check: Roblox confirming a player's age, through Facial Age Estimation or ID verification.
terms.terminal punctuation: Marks that end a sentence: period, question mark, exclamation mark. Presets must not use them.
terms.rate limit: A cooldown on how often something can be sent. Here, one preset per 10 seconds.
terms.encode: Hide a message in a code, like using numbers to stand for letters. Not allowed in presets.
terms.slang: Casual words whose meaning can change or be hidden. Presets must avoid it.
terms.Universe: Your whole game, including all of its places.

watchOut: Writing presets as questions or greetings. Keep them to short gameplay actions like "Attack" or "Follow me".
Adding punctuation like "Ready!". Leave off end marks so presets do not look like normal chat.
Offering more than 12 presets, or letting players spam them. Cap at 12 and add a 10-second cooldown.
Skipping filtering because you wrote the text yourself. Presets still must go through `TextService:FilterStringAsync()`.
Making presets look exactly like regular chat. Label them as system preset and style them differently.
Building your own when Quick Words would do. Quick Words already follows these rules.
